newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia cuts weekend work hours on Avella.
newsitem.headline: Kia cuts weekend work hours on Avella.

text.p: South Korean carmaker Kia Motors Corp has cut weekend work hours on some assembly lines for its Avella sub-compact cars because of high inventories, a Kia official said on Saturday.
Kia has given up the usual extra four-hour operations of lines for the domestic version of Avella on every other Saturday, the official said.
"The decision was made due to high inventories on the model," he said. "But we don't think this can be called a cut-back of work hours."
He said domestic sales of Avella cars were slowing, but gave no details.
"We will work only for four hours every Saturday, and we have not yet decided on until when this decision will be in effect," he said.
In the past, Kia employees worked for eight hours on alternate Saturdays and for four hours on the other Saturdays.
He said operations of lines for the company's other models, such as Sephia, Credos and Potentia, would not be affected.
The nation's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co, a decided to stop lines for extra work hours every day.
Hyundai's decision was also attributed by the company officials to high inventories because of slowing sales.
